summary: MarsLab is a browser-based Mars exploration and research workspace that brings planetary data, interactive 3D visualization, mission-planning exercises, and science education into one application. It uses the Mars Global Surveyor Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) dataset from NASA’s Planetary Data System to provide a low-resolution global topography preview, while preserving source metadata, coordinate conventions, and no-data gaps. The project also catalogs the USGS Astrogeology Mars 2020 HiRISE digital terrain model for Jezero and includes a validation and ingestion pipeline for a derived regional preview; the large source raster is not included in the public deployment. Users can explore referenced locations, design a conceptual base, plan routes for an educational rover, run reproducible simulations, follow guided lessons, and compile a source-linked research dossier. Simulated outputs are clearly distinguished from measured data. MarsLab is an independent project and is not affiliated with NASA.
